_provenance.note: Rhode Island dated facts. Because Rhode Island has NO existing packages/snap-rules StatePolicy entry, there is no engine constant to cross-check against — every entry below is either a routine COLA-cycle reminder, a disclosed research gap, or a warning about a fact this pack found time-sensitive or single-sourced.

entries.warning: dhs.ri.gov's own hosted copy of the full 218-RICR-20-00-1 regulation PDF (dhs.ri.gov/media/7796/download) is dated August 2024 and contains REDLINED, struck-through-old/inserted-new dollar figures from an FFY2023-to-FFY2024 rulemaking amendment (e.g. resource limits render as a garbled literal string combining the old $4,250/$2,750 figures with the new $4,500/$3,000 figures; the standard deduction table shows FFY2023-24 figures, not current FFY2026 figures). This pack explicitly did NOT rely on any dollar figure from this PDF and instead cross-verified every current dollar figure against DHS's separately-fetched, correctly-dated FFY2026 SNAP Annual Cost of Living Adjustment PDF (effective October 1, 2025) and DHS's live Eligibility & How to Apply page. This pack DID rely on this PDF's structural/procedural (non-dollar) text — categorical eligibility mechanics, resource-test exemptions, vehicle-exclusion rules, deduction methodology, certification-period rules — none of which showed comparable redlining. Before restating any dollar figure from a fresh fetch of this specific PDF, re-verify it is not still showing a stale redlined figure.

A secondary source (WorkWORLD) claims vehicles beyond Rhode Island's 2-vehicle exclusion cap are counted as a resource only above a $4,650 fair-market-value threshold. This pack could NOT locate this specific figure anywhere in Rhode Island's own primary regulation text (218-RICR-20-00-1 § 1.5.5) during its research and flags it as UNCONFIRMED — this pack's income-and-resources supplement states the 2-vehicle cap itself (which IS primary-source confirmed) but does not assert the $4,650 figure. Re-verify directly against § 1.5.5 or a DHS caseworker manual before treating this specific dollar threshold as settled.

This pack's restaurant-meals-program supplement states Rhode Island's RMP currently spans nine participating Subway restaurants, per DHS's own Online Purchasing & Restaurant Meals Program page — this pack did not independently enumerate or verify the specific nine locations, and that count could change without this pack's knowledge. Re-verify the current count and specific locations directly against DHS's page before restating this figure with full confidence in a high-stakes context (e.g. an applicant asking which specific restaurant to visit).

This pack's abawd-work-requirement supplement states Rhode Island delayed its OBBBA ABAWD rollout to March 1, 2026 for newly-affected ABAWDs, per DHS's own ABAWDs FAQ updated January 7, 2026. As of this pack's verification date (8/12/2026), March 1, 2026 is already in the past — the rollout has happened. Re-verify against DHS's current ABAWDs page before restating this March 1, 2026 date as a still-relevant future milestone; a household asking about ABAWD status today should be told their actual current countable-month count, which this pack cannot determine without their specific case history, exactly as DHS's own FAQ itself repeatedly cautions.

This pack's conclusion that Rhode Island currently has NO active area-wide ABAWD waiver rests on USDA FNS/FNA's ABAWD Time Limit Waivers FY 2025-2029 index showing no FY2026 Rhode Island entry (most recent entry FY2025, dated 03/12/2025) — this pack did not find a single DHS page stating Rhode Island's current waiver status in as many words. Re-check https://www.fna.usda.gov/snap/abawd/waivers/2025-2029 directly before restating this with full confidence beyond this window.

This pack's confirmed dollar figures (Standard Deduction $209/$209/$209/$223/$261/$299, Standard Utility Allowance $844, Standard Telephone Allowance $26, Maximum/Excess Shelter Deduction $744, Homeless Shelter Deduction $198.99, Standard Medical Deduction $183, minimum benefit $24, resource limits $3,000/$4,500, and the income-eligibility table by household size at 185%/200% FPG) are drawn from Rhode Island DHS's SNAP Annual Cost of Living Adjustment PDF effective October 1, 2025, matching the current FFY2026 cycle (October 1, 2025 - September 30, 2026). The FFY2027 COLA cycle begins October 1, 2026 — under two months from this pack's fetch date. Check dhs.ri.gov's SNAP Updates page or a fresh SNAP Annual Cost of Living Adjustment PDF after that date before restating any Rhode Island-specific dollar figure with full confidence.

This pack's program-identity supplement mentions the December 2024 RIBridges ransomware data breach and subsequent 2025 phased relaunch/settlement as resolved historical context, not a current operative barrier — every direct fetch this pack performed of dhs.ri.gov and the underlying RIBridges-linked pages returned clean, normal responses throughout this pack's research window (8/12/2026). If a future user report or fresh fetch shows portal instability, treat that as a NEW issue, not a recurrence of the 2024 breach, and re-verify current portal status directly rather than assuming this pack's 'resolved' characterization still holds indefinitely.
